title: The Imperative Mood
description: The present and aorist imperative, active, middle and passive, prohibitions with μή, and the imperative of εἰμί.

blocks.caption: Summary
blocks.html:
The imperative has only a second and a third person; English renders the third person with let: λυέτω, let him loose. The present imperative is formed on the present stem, the aorist active and middle on the aorist stem (with -σα, but no augment), the aorist passive on the aorist passive stem (-θη-). The tenses differ not in time but in kind of action: λῦσον is simply loose; λῦε is keep loosing, loose again and again. Second aorists take the endings of the present: λίπε, λιπέτω. εἰπέ and ἐλθέ have an irregular accent, and the second aorist middle λιποῦ is accented on the ending.

A prohibition uses μή with the present imperative or with the aorist subjunctive, never with the aorist imperative: μὴ λύε or μὴ λύσῃς, do not loose; μὴ λυέτω or μὴ λύσῃ, let him not loose. The first person (let us …) is the subjunctive you already know: ποιήσωμεν, let us do; μὴ ποιήσωμεν, let us not do.

ὅστις, ἥτις, ὅ τι, whoever, is used almost only in the nominative, sometimes nearly like ὅς. ὅσος, as great as, as many as, often stands with ἄν or ἐάν: ὅσα ἐὰν εἴπωσιν, whatever things they say.

blocks.caption: The imperative of λύω
rows: Second aorist of λείπω: active λίπε, λιπέτω, λίπετε, λιπέτωσαν; middle λιποῦ, λιπέσθω, λίπεσθε, λιπέσθωσαν.
Present imperative of εἰμί: ἴσθι, ἔστω, ἔστε, ἔστωσαν.
Contract verbs contract as usual: φίλει, φιλείτω, φιλεῖτε, φιλείτωσαν; middle and passive φιλοῦ, φιλείσθω, φιλεῖσθε, φιλείσθωσαν.

blocks.caption: Third-declension nouns of this lesson
blocks.html: οὖς, ὠτός, τό, an ear (dative plural ὠσί(ν)); ὕδωρ, ὕδατος, τό, water; φῶς, φωτός, τό, light; σκότος, σκότους, τό, darkness (like γένος). γῆ, γῆς, ἡ, earth, has the circumflex throughout because it is contracted.

blocks.caption: Common confusion
blocks.html: λύσατε (aorist imperative) and λύσετε (future indicative) differ in one vowel; ἐλύσατε (with augment) is the aorist indicative. λῦσαι is both the aorist middle imperative (loose for yourself) and the aorist active infinitive (to loose), told apart by the context. λύθητι, λυθήτω look like λυθῇ, λυθῇς (subjunctive) but have -θη- followed by -τι, -τω. μὴ λύσῃς (subjunctive) is a prohibition; μὴ λῦσον is never used.
